explanation_text: Let uncompensated syatem, [latex]T(s)=\frac{900}{s(s+1)(s+9)} [/latex] Phase crossover frequency of uncompensated system [latex]=(\omega _{pc})[/latex], at this frequency phase of [latex]T(j \omega )[/latex] is [latex]-180^{\circ}[/latex] Put   [latex] s=j\omega \text{ in }  T(s) [/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} T(j\omega )&=\frac{900}{j\omega (j\omega +1)(j\omega +9)} \\ \angle T(j\omega )&=-90^{\circ}-tan ^{-1}\omega -tan^{-1}\left ( \frac{\omega }{9} \right ) \\ \text{At, } & (\omega _{pc})_1,\angle T(j\omega )=-180^{\circ}\\ -180^{\circ}&=-90^{\circ}-tan^{-1}(\omega _{pc})_1 -tan^{-1}\left ( \frac{(\omega _{pc})_1}{9} \right )\\ -90^{\circ}&=tan^{-1}\frac{(\omega _{pc})_1+\frac{(\omega _{pc})_1}{9}}{1-\frac{(\omega _{pc})^2_1}{9}} \\ \Rightarrow 1-\frac{(\omega _{pc})^2_1}{9}&=0 \\ \Rightarrow (\omega _{pc})_1&= 3 \text{ rad/sec}   \end{aligned}[/latex] Gain cross frequency of compensated system, [latex](\omega _{gc})_2[/latex]= phase cross frequency of uncompensated system, [latex](\omega _{pc})_1[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \;\;(\omega _{gc})_2=(\omega _{gc})_1=\; 3[/latex]  rad/sec Phase-margin   [latex]=180^{\circ}+\angle T(j\omega )|_{\omega =(\omega _{gc})_2} [/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \; \; \;  45^{\circ}=180^{\circ}+\angle T(j\omega )|_{\omega =(\omega _{pc})_2} [/latex] At     [latex] (\omega _{gc})_2=3[/latex] rad/sec, phase angle of [latex]\angle T(j\omega )[/latex] is [latex] -135^{\circ}[/latex] and phase of uncompensated systen is [latex]-180^{\circ}[/latex] at 3 rad/sec. Hence option (D) is correct.

Let uncompensated syatem,
[latex]T(s)=\frac{900}{s(s+1)(s+9)} [/latex]
Phase crossover frequency of uncompensated system [latex]=(\omega _{pc})[/latex], at this frequency phase of [latex]T(j \omega )[/latex] is [latex]-180^{\circ}[/latex]
Put [latex] s=j\omega \text{ in } T(s) [/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} T(j\omega )&=\frac{900}{j\omega (j\omega +1)(j\omega +9)} \\ \angle T(j\omega )&=-90^{\circ}-tan ^{-1}\omega -tan^{-1}\left ( \frac{\omega }{9} \right ) \\ \text{At, } & (\omega _{pc})_1,\angle T(j\omega )=-180^{\circ}\\ -180^{\circ}&=-90^{\circ}-tan^{-1}(\omega _{pc})_1 -tan^{-1}\left ( \frac{(\omega _{pc})_1}{9} \right )\\ -90^{\circ}&=tan^{-1}\frac{(\omega _{pc})_1+\frac{(\omega _{pc})_1}{9}}{1-\frac{(\omega _{pc})^2_1}{9}} \\ \Rightarrow 1-\frac{(\omega _{pc})^2_1}{9}&=0 \\ \Rightarrow (\omega _{pc})_1&= 3 \text{ rad/sec} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Gain cross frequency of compensated system, [latex](\omega _{gc})_2[/latex]= phase cross frequency of uncompensated system, [latex](\omega _{pc})_1[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \;\;(\omega _{gc})_2=(\omega _{gc})_1=\; 3[/latex] rad/sec
Phase-margin [latex]=180^{\circ}+\angle T(j\omega )|_{\omega =(\omega _{gc})_2} [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \; \; \; 45^{\circ}=180^{\circ}+\angle T(j\omega )|_{\omega =(\omega _{pc})_2} [/latex]
At [latex] (\omega _{gc})_2=3[/latex] rad/sec,
phase angle of [latex]\angle T(j\omega )[/latex] is [latex] -135^{\circ}[/latex] and phase of uncompensated systen is [latex]-180^{\circ}[/latex] at 3 rad/sec.
Therefore, the compensator provides phase lead of [latex]45^{\circ}[/latex] at the frequency of 3 rad/sec.
Let X dB is the gain provided by the compensator, so at gain cross frequency, [latex]|T(j\omega )|_{com}[/latex]=1 or 0 dB. Gain of uncompensated system [latex]=|T(j\omega )|_{un-com} =\frac{100}{\omega \sqrt{1+\omega ^2}\sqrt{1+\left ( \frac{\omega }{9} \right )^2}} [/latex]
[latex]|T(j\omega )|_{un-com}[/latex] in dB
[latex]\;=40-20 \log \omega -20 \log \sqrt{1+\omega ^2} -20 \log \sqrt{1+\left ( \frac{\omega }{9} \right )^2}[/latex]
Gain of compensated system,
[latex]|T(j\omega )|_{com}=X+|T(j\omega )_{un-com}| [/latex]
[latex]|T(j\omega )|_{com}[/latex] must be zero at gain cross frequency [latex](\omega _{gc})_2[/latex]
[latex] |T(j\omega_{gc} )_2|_{com}=X+40-20 \log (\omega _{gc})_2 -20 \log \sqrt{1+(\omega _{gc})^2_2}-20 \log \sqrt{1+\frac{(\omega _{gc})^2}{9^2}}=0 [/latex]
[latex]X+40-20 \log 3-20 \log \sqrt{1+3^2}-20 \log \sqrt{1+\left ( \frac{3}{9} \right )^2}=0 [/latex]
[latex]X=-20dB[/latex]
So, the compensator provides an attenuation od 20dB. Hence option (D) is correct.

subject: Signals and Systems - Z-Transform
explanation_text: [latex]G(z)=\alpha z^{-1}+\beta z^{-3}[/latex] For, low frequency [latex](z=1)\rightarrow G(1)=\alpha +\beta \;\;...(i)[/latex] For, high frequency [latex](z=-1)\rightarrow G(-1)=-(\alpha +\beta) \;\;...(ii)[/latex] For now, [latex]g(n)=\{0,\alpha ,0, \beta\}[/latex] For linear phase FIR filter, g(n) should be either even symmetric or odd symmetric about virtual y-axis. To, satisfy the above condition. CASE: (i) [latex]\alpha =- \beta[/latex] ( odd symmetric about virtual y-axis) But in this case, G(1)=G(-1)=0 i.e. at low frequency [latex]\Rightarrow \; G(z)=0[/latex] and at high frequency [latex]\Rightarrow \; G(z)=0[/latex] Thus in this case filter will be band-pass. CASE: (ii) [latex]\alpha = \beta[/latex] ( even symmetric about virtual y-axis) In this case, At low frequency [latex]\Rightarrow \; G(z)=2\alpha [/latex] and at high frequency [latex]\Rightarrow \; G(-1)=-2\alpha [/latex] Filter will be either all pass or band-stop. Now, [latex]\begin{aligned} G(e^{j\omega })&=\alpha (e^{-j\omega }+e^{-j 3 \omega }) \\ &=\alpha e^{-j2\omega }(e^{j\omega }+e^{-j\omega }) \\ &= 2\alpha e^{-j2\omega } \cos \omega \end{aligned}[/latex]
explanation_html:
[latex]G(z)=\alpha z^{-1}+\beta z^{-3}[/latex]
For, low frequency [latex](z=1)\rightarrow G(1)=\alpha +\beta \;\;...(i)[/latex]
For, high frequency [latex](z=-1)\rightarrow G(-1)=-(\alpha +\beta) \;\;...(ii)[/latex]
For now, [latex]g(n)=\{0,\alpha ,0, \beta\}[/latex]
For linear phase FIR filter, g(n) should be either even symmetric or odd symmetric about virtual y-axis.
To, satisfy the above condition.

CASE: (i) [latex]\alpha =- \beta[/latex]
( odd symmetric about virtual y-axis)
But in this case,
G(1)=G(-1)=0
i.e. at low frequency [latex]\Rightarrow \; G(z)=0[/latex] and at high frequency [latex]\Rightarrow \; G(z)=0[/latex]
Thus in this case filter will be band-pass.

CASE: (ii) [latex]\alpha = \beta[/latex]
( even symmetric about virtual y-axis)
In this case,
At low frequency [latex]\Rightarrow \; G(z)=2\alpha [/latex] and at high frequency [latex]\Rightarrow \; G(-1)=-2\alpha [/latex]
Filter will be either all pass or band-stop.
Now,
[latex]\begin{aligned} G(e^{j\omega })&=\alpha (e^{-j\omega }+e^{-j 3 \omega }) \\ &=\alpha e^{-j2\omega }(e^{j\omega }+e^{-j\omega }) \\ &= 2\alpha e^{-j2\omega } \cos \omega \end{aligned}[/latex]
